newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Fourteen die in Guatemala tourist plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Fourteen die in Guatemala tourist plane crash.

text.p: Fourteen people, 12 of them tourists, were killed when a small plane taking them to Guatemala's Mayan site of Tikal crashed in jungle on Friday, aviation officials said.

The plane belonged to local airline Transportes Aereos Profesionales (TAPSA); aviation authority officials said at least one of the passengers was a U.S. citizen. First reports said the other passengers were Guatemalan tourists.

Officials at the Guatemalan civil aviation authority said the Brazilian-made turboprop aircraft crashed about five miles (eight km) from its destination, the airport of Flores in Peten province near Guatemala's northern border with Mexico.

Flores is the airport serving Guatemala's world-famous Mayan temple site of Tikal. Every year, thousands of travelers from around the world visit the pre-Colombian stone shrines set in unspoiled rainforest.

The Embraer Bandeirantes plane was on a regular tourist flight from Guatemala City to Flores and crashed as it prepared to land, Juan Luis Munoz, head of operations at the aviation authority, said. He said 12 passengers and two crew members died and there were no reported survivors.

The crash was the second involving a Guatemalan aircraft in just over a year. On Aug. 9 of last year, a Boeing 737 belonging to the country's Aviateca airline slammed into a volcano in El Salvador, killing all 65 people aboard.

Friday's accident was also the second major disaster to hit Guatemala in the last month. On Oct. 16 at least 80 people were crushed to death at a soccer stadium in Guatemala City just before the kickoff of a World Cup qualifying soccer match between Guatemala and Costa Rica.
